label: delimiter / mid-original-phase steps, boosted when the first token is j, n, 0, f, e or h
explanation: Diffuse positive-candidate unit. 45% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (active on 23% of delimiter steps, 4.6x lift), and most of the rest is in the original phase at t=3..6. It almost never fires at t=0-1 or in the copy phase after the first output (copy phase holds 6% of mass, mostly at recall_idx 0-2). Which sequences it fires on depends on content, most strongly the first token: first_tok j (3.8x), n (3.3x), 0 (2.6x), f/e/h (about 2x). Second-position n and earlier w also raise the rate. On original steps, the inputs l/v/s/3 raise it. The top activations (about 0.39) are all <DEL> steps in short sequences beginning j n... or 0 n... It is weaker in long sequences (L=8-9). The predicate (delimiter or t=3..5, with first_tok in {j,n,0,f,e,h}) gets only about 0.40 F1 and 0.53 mass recall on dev. The unit looks like a distributed readout of sequence content, not a clean single feature. No predicate tried did better than about 0.40 F1.
